newsitem.title: UK: UK oil revenues at highest level for nearly 11 yrs.
newsitem.headline: UK oil revenues at highest level for nearly 11 yrs.

text.p: The United Kingdom's oil revenues rose to almost 40 million stg a day in October due to rising output and oil prices nearly 50 percent higher than a year ago, said the Royal Bank of Scotland Oil and Gas Index.
Daily revenues at 39.8 million stg were the highest since January 1986 and compare with 28 million stg in October 1995.

The price of Brent crude rose 7.3 percent in October to average $24.13 a barrel and was 49.9 percent up on the year. In sterling terms Brent rose 5.5 percent to 15.21 stg per barrel in October and was 49 percent higher than a year ago.
In cash terms oil prices were at their highest since the Gulf War.
Natural gas output rose sharply in October by 32.2 percent reflecting new fields coming onstream to meet demand from power stations as well as the expected seasonal increase.

Average daily value of gas production in October was 14.2 million stg, almost a third higher than a year ago. The combined effect lifted the Royal Bank Oil and Gas Index by 12.6 percent in October leaving it six percent above October 1995.
Combined oil and gas revenues were 54 million stg in October, 39.5 percent above October 1995.
There is little prospect of any substantial fall in prices in the short term, according to Stephen Boyle, the Bank's Head of Business Economics.

"Oil stocks remain far lower than is typical for this time of year, while there could be delays in refinery maintenance work. In the absence of the return of Iraqi crude the most significant short-term determinant of prices is the severity of the winter in North America and Europe," he said.

Oil production in October rose 4.6 percent or 116,000 barrels a day (bpd) to just over 2.6 million bpd, leaving production 4.4 percent down on an annual basis. The rise was due to completion of maintenance work and three new fields coming on-stream during the month.
